Given: contract.xml, the brief, the approval, run-1.xml (written by hand, decision D4) and run-2.xml with their logs, the diff a3d2b7d..12cb717 (76 files), AGENTS.md and the documents under models/architecture, and the output of status and check. Not read: HANDOFF.md and models/decisions. The requester added a list of points to examine and three known limitations (the hand-written start run, the untested signal path on Windows, CK5 not yet observed), which is more than the skill's hand-over allows; the findings below rest on the files and on probes, not on that list. Read in full: every file under src, the three skills, the method and topic documents, the schemas, the example contracts and the visible text of every brief. Covered by byte comparison and by reading the generator instead of line by line: packages/** (identical to skills/ apart from generated manifests and READMEs) and cli-reference.md. The style blocks of the HTML pages were not read. All four automated checks were rerun at 12cb717 and exited 0 (44 tests pass, 1 skipped); the log hashes of run-2 match the receipt. Behaviour was probed in throwaway repositories under the OS temp directory (19 probe scenarios) and by 17 mutations of the kernel, 11 of the examples and 6 of the packages and help text in a throwaway clone. Limits: the approval statement could not be compared with the conversation it quotes; K1 was judged by a targeted search of the GRACE 4 repository for some sixty distinctive lines, headings and identifiers and a comparison of file names, not by a full comparison; the interrupted-receipt path could not be exercised on Windows; CK5 is the owner's and was not performed. K5 has no rule file and so no Rule element: the kernel validates the contract and every XML record with xmllint-wasm against the published XSD files and a parser disagreement fails closed, so K5 is upheld, with the residue in F13.

Finding.Text: Step 5 of close fails open. When git cannot resolve the start revision, changedBetween returns undefined and evaluate reads that as an empty diff (`changedBetween(...) ?? []`), so no protected path is reported and close proceeds. Reproduced without touching any record: a change whose complete diff writes a protected file is refused in the full repository (protected path touched: src/secret/key.txt) and closes with exit 0 in a `git clone --depth 1` of the same repository; status there prints no `protected:` line and `next: close`. The same happens when a start receipt names a revision the repository does not have. evidence-records.md step 5 and authorization.md (Protected paths block) require a refusal; a diff that cannot be computed is not a diff that touches nothing. The `outside:` listing is lost the same way. No conformance test covers it.

close does not verify what the review covered. reviewObligation compares only candidate and revision; start-revision, end-revision and contract-sha256 of the review record are read and never used. Probe: a completed review whose start-revision equals HEAD (an empty diff), whose end-revision is a revision that does not exist and whose contract-sha256 is all zeros passes check without a defect and closes. evidence-records.md (Supersession, a review is repeated) says the current review must cover the complete diff to the final revision; the kernel holds the start revision and could compare it. The review skill names the natural way to get here: a re-review that covers the fix alone.

A blocking finding can be disposed of without the owner. evidence-records.md says a blocking finding is owner-disposed with the owner's quoted OwnerDecision, and AGENTS.md says no approval state is set by inference. review.xsd makes OwnerDecision optional, readReview does not read it, and close accepts status="owner-disposed" on its own. Probe: a review with one blocking finding marked owner-disposed and no OwnerDecision, and one marked resolved with no Resolution, passes check and closes. The only test of owner-disposed (receipts.test.ts, CLOSE review obligations) always supplies the element.

The surface is not exactly the one method.md lists (K2). The table says anything not in it is absent. The finding stands on packages/** alone: three generated harness packages with a plugin manifest, an OpenPackage manifest and READMEs, present and not in the table. Also present and not in it, listed for completeness: src/tools/package.ts, cli-reference.ts and examples-verify.ts with the package.json scripts package, package:verify and examples:verify; the `help` pseudo-command (`grace5 help close` exits 0) and the `--version` option. The same paragraph says no log parser beyond ordered substring matching, while trace.ts parses the provenance line into key and value fields as trace-provenance.md requires. The brief's own resolved findings treated K2 as exact when cli-reference.md and m2-proposal.md were added to the Documents row; packages and tools were not added. commands.md (Details settled in implementation) says a refusal is printed on standard error. Every command prints `refused:` with console.log on standard output; only usage errors go to standard error. Observed: `close` without a review writes "refused: no review" to stdout and nothing to stderr. The conformance helper merges both streams with the comment that the documents do not say which stream carries a refusal, so no test can notice.

Anything under .grace5/changes/ is outside the candidate and outside the dirty state, whatever it is. Probe: a check whose command runs a script kept in the change directory passed; the script was then changed to exit 1 and committed together with a new code file beside it; the candidate did not move, the result still counted and close succeeded. source-identity.md argues that the definition hash binds the contract's commands; it does not bind a file a command executes. The kernel matches the document here; the document leaves the hole, and nothing reports a check command or a Path that points into the change tree. A Protected glob under .grace5/changes/ can never be reported either.

A receipt can say dirty="false" for a working tree the candidate does not describe. Probes: with `git update-index --skip-worktree` on the product file, a gate that reads the working tree passed on content the committed candidate does not contain, was recorded clean and closed; a gate that depends on an ignored local file passed clean and closed. Both follow the definition of dirty in source-identity.md, which does not name these limits. Separately, dirtyPaths returns an empty list when `git status` itself fails, so a git error reads as a clean tree; this was read, not reproduced.

Defects that check reports do not hold run or close. Probe: an approval with two Bound elements for one check, one with a stale hash, and a brief that omits a protected path (the FS-14 defect) made check exit 1 with both defects, while status said `next: close` and close succeeded. Only contract defects and schema-invalid records make a change malformed. Step 1 of close asks that the approval binds every check and is satisfied by any one matching Bound. The prepare skill says the owner reads nothing while check reports a defect; nothing after the owner gate enforces it.

A change is closed when a file named close.xml exists. Probe on a change with no run and no review: an empty close.xml made status print both `malformed:` and `closed:` with `next: none, the change is closed`; a schema-valid close.xml written by hand made status and the listing report the change as closed with no defect, although its candidate, review and run do not exist. Ledger entry L-15 gives closure by record existence as the failure the close command exists to prevent. Records are agent-writable and the kernel cannot authenticate them, but status could at least compare the close record with the state it names.

Test adequacy. Every case id FS-01 to FS-14 and FL-01 to FL-09 has a test with exact-phrase assertions and, for most, a closing control; 13 mutations of the kernel aimed at 13 cases (FS-02, 03, 04, 06, 07, 08, 10, 11, 13, FL-04, 05, 07, 08) were each caught by the test of that case. Gaps: removing the `rule violated` refusal left the whole CLOSE test passing, and removing the `definition changed since the result` condition left the whole suite at 44 pass, 0 fail; no test names `review covers an earlier revision`, `approval does not bind check` or `recorded dirty`, although the kernel does issue each of them (all three probed). FL-01 on Windows runs only the kill-outright path, and its close assertion is `refused: .+` on a check that never had a result, so it would pass without any interruption handling; the receipt path (interrupted and not-attempted verdicts) is skipped on Windows and was not run in run-2. The rejected half of FL-04 and the CLOSED test also assert only `refused: .+`. A2 is met for the listed cases; A1 beyond those cases rests on the untested phrases above.

status reports `outside: .gitignore`. The change added the ignore rule for .grace5/changes/*/records/logs/. It is not a test of an affected file and the contract does not list it under Affected. The edit carries out what evidence-records.md says this repository does with logs and does nothing else, so it is justified in substance, but it is an unlisted write and should have been a Path. A consequence to weigh: the logs behind run-1 and run-2 exist only on the machine that ran them.

K5 residue. init.ts carries its own copy of the ChangeId pattern of common.xsd. contract.ts and records.ts restate schema defaults (required true, cwd ".", min 1, start false). The model is read by a second, hand-written XML reader (xml.ts) after xmllint has validated the text; where the two could disagree (DOCTYPE, CDATA, processing instructions, other encodings) the reader throws and the change is reported malformed, so the disagreement fails closed. With every example valid, examples:verify keeps passing if XSD validation is removed from readContract (tried); whether the suite would notice was not tried, and the FL-06 tests are the ones that feed the kernel an invalid contract.

Smaller observations. .grace5/README.md, a listed Path, still says that until the kernel exists changes are made by hand. retirement.md leaves G-12 (no verbatim copying) unchecked with the note to check it when code and skills exist; they now exist. A rerun that is killed outright leaves an earlier pass of the same check current and close proceeds, with only an `interrupted:` line in status (probed; it follows the supersession rule as written). When a log carries two provenance lines echoing the run, the last one wins, so a command that prints origin=replay and then origin=live is recorded as live (probed; within what trace-provenance.md leaves to review of the capture command). The hand-written run-1.xml lists a directory as Preexisting where the kernel lists each file.

Review.Adequacy: `bun run check` is `tsc --noEmit`. A pass separates a tree that type-checks from one that does not: an injected return-type error made it exit 2. That is a failure of A1 that CK2 cannot see, because Bun runs TypeScript without checking it, so kernel code with a type error can pass every test. The check discriminates that failure mode and no other: it says nothing about whether a command behaves as the documents state, and that part of A1 rests on CK2. This is a judgement on a narrow check that shares its criterion; read alone against A1 it would not discriminate.

`bun test` runs 45 black-box tests that drive the CLI as a subprocess in temporary git repositories and read the records as text. For A2 a pass discriminates: every conformance case has a test, and each of 13 mutations that made the kernel accept a case turned the test of that case red. For A1 it discriminates on the three check kinds and the five commands as far as the conformance cases and receipt fields go, and not for the refusals listed in F10 or the defects F1 to F3, which the suite does not reach. On Windows one test is skipped, so the pass of run-2 does not include the interrupted receipt.

In a throwaway clone it exited 1 for each of: a schema-invalid example contract, a criterion naming a missing check, a contract edited under its brief, a brief losing a decision, a trace limitation, an exclusion, the word count or gaining an open finding, a deleted example, the defective brief replaced by the sound one, the defective contract losing its protected paths, and a kernel that stops reporting an omitted protected path. Limits: it calls the functions, not the `grace5 check` command (FS-14 in CK2 does that); it skips the rule-path rule; and because every example is valid it would still pass if XSD validation were removed.
